_port_note: pick_request_kind chose one of three branches at build time; each branch has a different option set, so each is now its own card selected by its own condition. The branch that fired was invisible to content before — last_request_kind is a field with one writer and no reader outside the picker. tick:request — this card has no sweep and no pool draw. It is reachable only by CustomerRepSystem naming it when a request ages past CS_ESCALATE_AFTER_DAYS and the weekly ceiling has room. The ceiling is a Sales-side policy about the desk, not a tempo rule, so it stays in that system; what it lost is the ability to push. LOCKS ADDED. The old builders withheld these rows by not BUILDING them — the promise row was skipped when a word was already open, the discount row when the cap was spent. A card is data now, so the row exists and must lock instead, which is §17.5's ruling and the better behaviour: a row that disappears teaches the player nothing, a row that is greyed with its reason teaches them the rule. Ported without them, every request card would have minted unlimited promises and uncapped discounts through a channel the retention card had closed. `musteri.is_assigned` REMOVED from the condition. The old builder took the DESK LEAD, not the account's steward — `build_cs_request(c, reps[0])` — so the request channel never depended on the account having a named rep, and requiring one meant the card was refused at G7 for every founder-managed account while CustomerRepSystem's own log said it had escalated. The desk's policy (an aged request, budget left in the week, a staffed desk) stays where it belongs, in the system; what is left on the card is the BRANCH.
